Figures Announces $8.5 Million to Fix Runway at the Montgomery Airport | Representative Shomari Figures Skip to main content Figures Announces $8.5 Million to Fix Runway at the Montgomery Airport August 14, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures (AL-02), a member of the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, announced that over $8.5 million in federal funding has been awarded for renovations and improvements at the Montgomery Regional Airport. The funding will help strengthen core airport infrastructure while enhancing safety and operational efficiency. These improvements are critical to ensuring the airport can meet current needs, maintain compliance with federal standards, and support continued growth in passenger travel and business activity.  “I'm thrilled to see our community receive significant federal support and investment with over $8.5 million in federal funding,” said Congressman Figures.  “The Montgomery Regional Airport is essential to our local, state and regional economy, and this funding will help to make necessary infrastructure updates to improve conditions at the airport and ensure its long-term viability.” The $8,506,686 in federal funding comes through a Department of Transportation grant and will go toward rehabilitating over 9,000 feet of existing runway to enhance structural integrity, minimize debris, and extend the useful lifetime of the runway.  Congressman Figures sent a letter of support for the Montgomery Regional Airport to receive this funding in January of this year. To read the letter of support, click here .  Issues : Congress Media Press Releases In the News Back to top button

Figures Calls for Emergency Hearing on President Trump’s Beef Order | Representative Shomari Figures Skip to main content Figures Calls for Emergency Hearing on President Trump’s Beef Order August 31, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures (AL-02) sent a letter to House Agriculture Committee Chairman Glenn “GT" Thompson requesting a hearing to examine President Trump’s recent proclamation authorizing the import of 300,000 metric tons of foreign beef that can be sold below market-rate, a move that provides minimal to no relief to consumers while harming the long-term viability of local cattle farmers.  “The Administration has stated that the action is intended to address elevated beef prices and increase the supply of ground beef for American consumers,” Figures wrote.  “However, the decision has raised significant concerns among cattle producers, agricultural organizations, and consumers about what, if any, economic relief this policy will provide. Furthermore, industry stakeholders have raised concerns that the potential long-term negative impacts of this policy, including higher beef prices and forcing cattle farmers out of business, outweigh any short-term relief, which would be temporary and minimal at best.”   This move by President Trump comes at a time when farmers are already being hammered by the President’s war in Iran and retaliatory tariffs caused by the White House’s reckless trade policies.   In meetings with producers throughout the Second Congressional District, Congressman Figures has heard from those who are struggling, and in response, has pushed to help American farmers through legislation like the Tariff Impacted Farmer Support Act of 2026 , which would temporarily authorize up to $15 billion in relief for family farms. Congressman Figures is again standing up for Alabama farmers and demanding answers to the President’s order by calling for this hearing.     “The Committee has a responsibility to understand the implications of the Pre

Figures Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Establish Tuskegee Airmen Memorial in Washington, DC | Representative Shomari Figures Skip to main content Figures Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Establish Tuskegee Airmen Memorial in Washington, DC July 22, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures (AL-02) introduced the Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Act, a bill to create a memorial in Washington, DC, to commemorate the service, sacrifice, and enduring legacy of the Tuskegee Airmen.   “The Tuskegee Airmen are among the most heroic and consequential soldiers that our nation has ever had,” said Congressman Figures. “While facing horrific discrimination at home, these men risked their lives to defend rights and freedoms abroad. Their courage, skill, and unwavering dedication not only contributed to the Allied victory but also helped pave the way for the desegregation of the U.S. military. Their contributions to our country deserve to be memorialized in our nation’s capital, and I'm proud to introduce this bipartisan bill to make that a reality.”   " The introduction of this authorizing legislation in Congress is a vital milestone in our ongoing mission to preserve and honor the legacy of our nation’s pioneering heroes,” said Ms. Angela Holmes, 1st Vice President for Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. "We extend our deepest gratitude to Representative Shomari Figures and our congressional partners for championing this effort. As we see the final generation of our original members passing, establishing a permanent landmark in Washington, D.C., ensures that their monumental contributions to military integration, excellence, and civil rights will never be forgotten by future generations.”  Congressman Figures’ bill would authorize Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated to establish a memorial on federal land in the District of Columbia. This is a key, necessary first step towards making this well-deserved memorial a reality. Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated is a national nonprofit founded to preserve the history and achievements of the original Tuskegee Airmen and engage with youth to inspire future careers in aviation, aerospace and STEM.

Figures (AL-02) introduced the   Tariff Impacted Farmer Support Act of 2026 to provide targeted financial relief and support for farmers who produce cotton, peanuts, soybeans, corn, and poultry.  Farmers across Alabama and the nation continue to face rising production costs, market volatility, and economic uncertainty that have placed extraordinary pressure on family farming operations. These challenges are compounded by retaliatory tariffs resulting from the Trump Administration's trade policies. For farmers operating on thin margins, a single year of substantial losses can threaten the long-term viability of their operations.  “Alabama farmers are the backbone of our economy and of rural communities throughout the state,” said Congressman Figures. “Amid incredibly difficult economic challenges, farmers have repeatedly demonstrated their resilience and grit, but many smaller operations lack the financial reserves necessary to withstand prolonged market disruptions, lost export sales, and the uncertainty created by President Trump’s tariffs.
